text: Generative AI for game development. Types of interactive narratives. Six ways players live inside a story and which one's generative AI supercharges. Hello, this is Liam in forbear. When people hear interactive narrative, they picture dialogue choices. Choices are one delivery system. This chapter maps six and shows which one's generative AI supercharges. Six terms, then we're off. Branching narrative choices split the story into paths. Open-ended, the story emerges from exploration. Procedural systems generate story on the fly. Dialogue-driven conversation is the mechanic. Environmental, the world tells the story. Hybrid, all of the above, layered. Last chapter was the blueprint. How stories are structured. The story. Moment to moment. Choice by choice. Same bones, different question. Six delivery systems. Branching. Your choices fork the plot. Open-ended. The world is the plot. Procedural. The plot writes itself. Dialogue driven talk is action. Environmental, the set is the script. Hybrid, everything at once. Why learn all six? Because the structure you choose decides your workload, your players freedom, and critically where generative AI can actually help match the tool to the story. Branching at key moments, the player chooses, and the story splits. Some branches rejoin the main road. Others drive off a cliff into a completely different ending. The Walking Dead by Telltale. Every lie,

Every mercy, every abandonment is tracked and thrown back at you episodes later. Best for narrative RPGs and moral dilemmas. The price writing multiplies with every fork. This is where AI earns its keep. It generates the variations, alternate dialogue, consequences, scene rewrites, and fills the gaps between branches so the story stays coherent no matter which fork the player took. Open-ended, no chapters, no missions, just a world. The story arrives in fragments. A rumor, a ruin, a stranger's warning. You assemble it by living in it. Skyrim, hundreds of hours, no required path. Best for open worlds and explorers. The win is freedom. The risk is drift without structure. The story

Can dissolve into tourism. AI populates the emptiness. Contextual lore, side quests, ambient dialogue, world events, all generated from how the player explores. The world feels reactive even where nothing was handwritten. Procedural. Nothing is pre-written. Algorithms and AI systems generate narrative fragments, traits, and events on the fly, and your actions decide how they combine. AI dungeon type anything, and the story continues. No branches because nothing was written. Best for sandboxes and improvisers. Infinite variety. The risk is incoherence. The perfect AI fit. Language models generate the seeds, encounters, and events while anchoring them to character goals, and world themes so the improvisation stays coherent. Dialogue-driven conversation is the gameplay. You pick a tone,

Diplomatic, aggressive, curious, and the world answers in kind, shifting attitudes, and redirecting the plot. Mass Effect, the dialogue wheel shapes shepherd, diplomat, or soldier in relationships, loyalty, even romances follow, best for character RPGs. The cost, every branch needs writing, and too many choices exhaust the player. AI's home turf. It writes the variations, shifts emotional tone, adapts NPC personalities, and reacts to what the player actually said. Cutting the writing workload that used to make this structure so expensive. Environmental, no dialogue trees, no cutscenes. The story is in the bloodstain, the broken photo, the graffiti, and you're the detective. Miss the clue, miss the story. Gone home, one

House, one family's history, zero combat. Learned entirely by snooping. Best for mystery and horror. The risk players walk right past the story. AI becomes the set dresser. It generates the notes, logs, graffiti, and item descriptions and places them where your exploration pattern will actually find them. Hybrid all of it layered. A linear spine for the main story. Branching missions, environmental depth in every room, and procedural events filling the gaps between. Red Dead Redemption 2, a linear epic wrapped in dialogue missions, random encounters, and environments that tell their own stories. Best for AAA worlds. The cost, enormous resources, and tone is hard to hold together. Here, AI is the glue.

Dynamic dialogue for linear missions, emerging events for the open world, procedural side quests, adaptive lore, holding the layers together so the seams don't show. Side by side, branching trades, writing for agency, open-ended trades, structure for freedom, procedural trades, coherence for infinity, dialogue trades, brevity for intimacy. The table isn't a ranking, it's a menu. In the AI suitability matrix, procedural and dialogue driven are a very high fit. That's what language models do. Branching, open-ended, and hybrid are high.
